messages.subject: shiny + gridSVG highly interactive plot
parts:
Is it possible to build a web application that can interact with element in the plot?
Say, when click on a certain point in a scatter plot, then the value of the point will be shown under the plot in the form of a table? The effect:

I am quite new to R, the current code of my application (jquery file, to be specific) is refer to svgfiller.js of Timely Portfolio, but apparently insufficient to realise the expected function.

My current code:


server.R

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  

  data = reactive({

    

    inFile = input$file1

    

    if (is.null(inFile))

      return("No file selected")

    

    read.csv(inFile$datapath, header=input$header, sep=input$separator,quote=input$quote)

  })

   

  plotchoice = reactive({

    paste(input$demonstratePlot,"showplot",sep=".")

  })

  

  output$classUI = renderUI({

    selectInput("classlabel","Classify by:", c=featurelist())

  })

  

  output$datapreview = renderTable({

    head(data())

  })

  

  output$svg.grid = reactive({

      pr = princomp(iris[1:4])

      group = iris[,5]

      inst = nrows(iris)

      #xyplot

      xyPlot.showplot = 

        xyplot(pr$scores[,1] ~ pr$scores[,2],

               group = group,

               panel = customPanel,

               key=list(rect=list(col=trellis.par.get("superpose.symbol")$col[1:2]),

                        text=list(label=levels(group))))      

    print(get(plotchoice()))

      for (i in 1:inst) {

        grid.garnish(paste("point", i, sep="."), group = FALSE)

      }

    tempsvg <- tempfile(fileext=".svg")

    on.exit(unlink(tempsvg)) 

    gridToSVG(name=tempsvg)

    svgoutput <- readLines(tempsvg, n=-1)

    svgoutput

  }) 

})


dynamicPanel.js

<script>

var networkOutputBinding = new Shiny.OutputBinding();

$.extend(networkOutputBinding, {

    find: function(scope) {

      return $(scope).find('.shiny-network-output');

    },

    renderValue: function(el,data) {

          $(el).html(data.join(''));      

    }

  });

Shiny.outputBindings.register(networkOutputBinding, 'output.networkbinding');

</script>

$extend(networkInputBinding,{
  find:function(scope){
    return $(scope).find('#point');
  },
  $('#point').click(function(){
  $(this).hide();
  });
})
